title: Ethiopian Fried Fish Sandwich
community: Lakeside towns — the fish sandwich of Hawassa and Bahir Dar
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Fried Fish Sandwich — berbere-marinated fried Nile perch in a baguette-style roll with silsi, berbere mayo, pickled jalapeños, and fresh tomato. The modern street food of Hawassa and Bahir Dar lakeside towns — the fish sandwich that makes the most of the freshest catch.
longDesc: The Ethiopian fried fish sandwich is the lakeside town's modern street food — combining the berbere fried Nile perch tradition with the sandwich format popular in Ethiopian urban culture.
steps: Marinate fish in berbere, lemon, garlic, and salt for 15 minutes.
Fry as per ETH082 method until golden.
Split rolls. Spread berbere mayo on both sides.
Top with sliced tomato, pickled jalapeño, and coriander.
chefTips: The berbere mayo is the element that makes this distinctly Ethiopian.
Serve immediately — the hot fish wilts the bread quickly.
cookingScience: See ETH082 for fried fish science.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh lakeside fish — shortest possible supply chain.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian fried fish sandwich is lakeside Ethiopia's contemporary street food — combining the country's freshwater fish tradition with the urban sandwich culture that has become part of Ethiopian food life. Eating one while watching hippos in Lake Hawassa is a quintessentially modern Ethiopian experience.
